## **Walden School — Independent K–12 Private School in Louisville, Kentucky**

[Discover Walden](https://walden-school.org/admissions)

# Who we are

Walden School is an independent, progressive K–12 private school in Louisville, Kentucky, serving students from Kindergarten through 12th grade. Located in St. Matthews, Walden combines small classes, personalized instruction, inquiry-based learning, and a close-knit community to help students thrive academically, creatively, and personally.

For more than 50 years, Walden has provided a college-preparatory education designed to develop curious, confident, compassionate, and independent thinkers. Students have opportunities to pursue rigorous academics, the arts, athletics, leadership, and service throughout their K–12 experience.

## Why Families Choose Walden

Families choose Walden for its individualized approach to education, small classes, strong relationships between students and teachers, and supportive K–12 community.

**Walden offers:**

*   Kindergarten through 12th grade

*   Small class sizes and individualized attention

*   Inquiry-based and hands-on learning

*   College-preparatory academics

*   AP and AP Capstone opportunities

*   Fine and performing arts

*   K–12 athletics

*   Service learning and leadership opportunities

*   Dedicated college counseling

*   Financial aid for qualifying families

## A K–12 Education Built Around the Individual Student

Rather than treating every student the same, Walden teachers get to know students as individuals and adapt instruction to challenge and support them. Students are encouraged to ask questions, explore their interests, collaborate with others, and take ownership of their learning.

## **Walden School — Independent K–12 Private School in Louisville, Kentucky**

[Discover Walden](https://walden-school.org/admissions)

# Who we are

Walden School is an independent, progressive K–12 private school in Louisville, Kentucky, serving students from Kindergarten through 12th grade. Located in St. Matthews, Walden combines small classes, personalized instruction, inquiry-based learning, and a close-knit community to help students thrive academically, creatively, and personally.

For more than 50 years, Walden has provided a college-preparatory education designed to develop curious, confident, compassionate, and independent thinkers. Students have opportunities to pursue rigorous academics, the arts, athletics, leadership, and service throughout their K–12 experience.

## Why Families Choose Walden

Families choose Walden for its individualized approach to education, small classes, strong relationships between students and teachers, and supportive K–12 community.

**Walden offers:**

*   Kindergarten through 12th grade

*   Small class sizes and individualized attention

*   Inquiry-based and hands-on learning

*   College-preparatory academics

*   AP and AP Capstone opportunities

*   Fine and performing arts

*   K–12 athletics

*   Service learning and leadership opportunities

*   Dedicated college counseling

*   Financial aid for qualifying families

## A K–12 Education Built Around the Individual Student

Rather than treating every student the same, Walden teachers get to know students as individuals and adapt instruction to challenge and support them. Students are encouraged to ask questions, explore their interests, collaborate with others, and take ownership of their learning.

## Developing Curious Thinkers

Chance School, a private school in the heart of Glenview in Louisville, KY, serves children from preschool through 5th grade. Our educators thoughtfully develop the whole child through Progressive Education, offering a rigorous, inquiry-based program that cultivates curiosity, academic excellence, leadership, teamwork, and resilience, preparing students to become confident, lifelong leaders who flourish in an ever-evolving world.

## Letter from the Head of School Stephanie Medcalfe

![Image 4: Stephanie Medcalfe Image](https://3.files.edl.io/e447/26/05/29/214714-2d396dfc-fbb5-4f61-b910-f026a8ab6ca1.png)

I am delighted to introduce you to Virginia Chance School, where we prioritize not only strong academic achievement but also the overall development of your child.

We excel at creating a collaborative environment that instills self-motivation, a growth mindset, and critical thinking skills in our students.

Our focus on nurturing a love of learning through hands-on exploration and teamwork, in engaging classrooms and on a beautiful wooded campus, is ideal for children ready for the unique rigor of the Chance School.

Choosing the right educational path for your child is a significant decision, and I invite you to experience firsthand the captivating educational opportunities that await your child at Chance School.

Together, we can foster a lifelong love of learning and personal growth.

At Chance, we embrace a progressive education approach that is evidence-based and recognized for its innovative, inquiry-focused curriculum. The curricular foundation blends the school’s philosophy with age-appropriate milestones, Common Core Standards, and guidelines from our accrediting bodies, ISACS, NAEYC, the Gesell Institute, and academic best practices.

Each day, your child will have the opportunity to explore, discover, and develop meaningful connections with their peers and the world around them. Welcome! We can't wait to get to know your family and share what makes Virginia Chance School so magical!

Tales from Under the Trees   
  
Beneath a canopy of whispering leaves, a pitcher of sunshine-yellow lemonade became an act of kindness, imagination, and wonder. To an adult, it may look like simple play. To a child, it is storymaking.  
  
Storymaking is how children make sense of their world. It allows them to explore ideas, emotions, relationships, and adventures in a way that feels natural and joyful. When children create imaginary worlds, characters, and adventures, they are weaving together experiences, strengthening problem- solving skills, developing empathy, and nurturing creativity. Through imagination, they discover that they are not merely participants in the world—they are creators within it. Through these small moments, children become authors of their own learning.  
  
And perhaps most importantly, storymaking preserves something precious: the ability to believe that the world is full of possibilities.  
  
The lemonade was not for friends or family; it was for a bear. The child had never actually seen the bear. No pawprints marked the ground, and no rustling shape moved between the trees. Yet the child knew what it liked to drink and how thirsty it might be.  
  
Whether the bear ever comes is beside the point. The magic was already there, the moment the child believed it might be.  
  
Last week, our Summer Under the Trees camp was transformed into a world of wonder and imagination as children stepped into the role of Enchanted Explorers.  
  
With colorful ribbons dancing in the breeze, little hands crafted magical wands ready for woodland adventures. Nearby, a busy lemonade stand appeared, serving refreshing drinks to the "forest bears" who had wandered into our imaginary world. Fairy wings fluttered as children twirled, danced, and celebrated the magic of summer beneath the trees.  
  
At Virginia Chance School, we believe childhood is a time for curiosity, creativity, and joyful discovery. Through imaginative play and meaningful experiences in nature, children create stories, build friendships, and develop a deeper connection to the world around them.

Discovering the Secret Sounds of Plants  
  
🌿✨ Have you ever wondered if plants can "speak"? During a recent exploration, children asked, "Do flowers have a sound?" Instead of giving a quick answer, we embraced their curiosity with a magical journey using PlantWave technology.  
  
PlantWave lets us listen to the subtle electrical signals of plants, transforming them into music! 🎶 Our students were excited to share their theories on how a dead plant might sound compared to a living one. From no sound to slow, melodious tunes to lively, happy beats, their imaginations ran wild.  
  
They wondered what else around us might be communicating in ways we can’t see or hear and requested to go around our campus and discover what else could make music! We made so many beautiful discoveries. Moments like this remind us that the world is more alive than we often realize.🌱💡  
  
This lesson was a blend of science and imagination, encouraging young minds to think beyond what they can see or hear and to remain open to the wonders of nature. 🌞

Embracing the Elements: What It Means to Be a 'Chance Kid' 🌧️🎒  
Remember the joy of splashing in puddles or playing in the mud as a child? Whether you loved it or hesitated at the thought of wet socks, these moments shaped us. At Chance School, we believe in creating these core memories for our Chance Kids and building resilience along the way.  
  
Tough Temperatures Build Resilience ❄️  
This winter taught us a lot! Our gear kept us warm, but frigid temperatures tested our limits. At times, friends would come up right away to ask, "When are we going inside?" While we want to be sure children are safe, we allow for moments of discomfort and flexibility, giving our friends ideas of how they can stay warm on a cold day through racing, climbing, and laughing.  
  
Messy Conditions Build Flexibility 🌿  
Our friends have grown through messy, outdoor play. A wet sock in a boot? No problem, just pull that boot off and ditch the sock. Just remember to bring it inside with you. Speaking of inside, teachers learn flexibility too, with helping to transition from outerwear once inside. We learn to take it in stride and make time for the cleanup. It can add stress, but we breathe through it and, more importantly, laugh through it.  
  
Living With a Little Discomfort Teaches Patience 🌧️  
On days when the temperatures are safe for getting wet (we look forward to a lot more of these in the springtime), we push ourselves to live in the moment and cherish the learning that only happens when you stop controlling the elements and start embracing them. Dry clothes are waiting for us inside, thanks to our thoughtful Moms and Dads. We are safe. Let's feel how those drops of rain coat our hair and sprinkle in our eyes.  
  
A Special Thank You to the Missing Socks 🧦  
To all the missing socks, mittens, and hats- thank you for being part of our journey. While we do our best to reunite you with your owners, sometimes you become little heroes lost in the adventure. Keep labeling, and we'll keep looking!  
  
Join us in celebrating the resilience, flexibility, and patience of our Chance Kids as we continue to make memories, one raindrop at a time. 🌈- Pre-K Teachers Ms. Julia & Ms. Brooke

Building Trust 🌟  
An excerpt from a Preschool Threes Newsletter:  
  
"Trust is all about consistency! When expectations are not consistent, children can become easily confused. This confusion will lead to them testing more boundaries and even power struggles. It is important that we set clear expectations for what is expected versus unexpected behavior at a given place or time. This is work that we start on day one and take very seriously because we understand the why behind it. As teachers and parents, it is our job to be the constant. This means we must follow through with what we say will happen in a certain situation. This is how we build trust.  
  
Consistency is Key:  
  
Lunch: Encourage keeping hands to themselves. “Bothering friends or touching their food is not a good choice, we will have to find a more successful spot for you to sit. We keep our hands to ourselves at lunch.”  
  
Outdoor Play: Safety first! “It is not safe when you poke someone with a stick, show us the safe way to play with sticks or they will be closed to you.”  
  
At school, unless it's a serious safety concern, we give two reminders before any consequences. Following through is crucial - empty words break trust.  
  
Follow Through with Few Words:   
  
“Not safe. Sticks are closed now.”  
  
Acknowledge feelings: “I know you’re sad, but sticks are closed. Try again tomorrow.”  
  
At lunch, after reminders: “I’m going to help you find a more successful spot to eat.”  
  
Our forever hope is that when we share this kind of information with you, it helps support your hard work at home. Preschool Teachers- Ms. Jensen & Ms. Katie"

The Power of How We Speak: A Journey in Tone  
  
🌟 Room 1 Pre-K Update: Embracing the Power of Tone 🌟  
This week, we embarked on an exciting journey to understand the importance of our tone of voice. Our children have been doing an amazing job expressing their big feelings with words. Now, we’re focusing on how to deliver those words with care and empathy.  
  
Discovering the Meaning of "Tone"  
Before diving in, we asked the children what "tone" means to them. Here are their insightful thoughts:  
“It’s the way your words sound.” — Camden  
“It’s how you hear it and feel it.” — Ace  
“Sometimes it’s too loud.” — Roman  
“It’s how you know someone is happy or mad.” — Walker  
  
As our young learners grow, so do their communication skills. At ages 4 and 5, they are learning the art of using their words thoughtfully. A loud or unkind tone can unintentionally upset others, turning small issues into big ones.  
  
Listening Beyond the Words  
To illustrate the power of tone, we role-played scenarios. We used the phrase, “Hey, you broke my train track!” in two different tones: one angry and one calm. The children noticed the difference:  
“When you yelled, it made me not want to listen.” — Rihaan  
“They were the same but they made me feel different.” — Remi  
“When you said it happy, it made me feel happy and calm.” — Roman  
“The mean tone made me feel scared.” — Ella  
“Yeah, the loud tone made me feel shy.” — Davis  
We encouraged them to try using different tones, facial expressions, and body language, learning that how we say something can change the meaning, even if the words remain the same.  
  
Moments of Love, Play, and Careful Communication  
In moments of frustration, we emphasized awareness over correction, using gentle reminders like “tone check” and “redo!” This empowers the children to recognize the power of their words and offers them a chance to express themselves as they truly intend to.  
  
Join us in celebrating these beautiful moments of growth, love, and learning. 💬✨

## Developing Curious Thinkers

Chance School, a private school in the heart of Glenview in Louisville, KY, serves children from preschool through 5th grade. Our educators thoughtfully develop the whole child through Progressive Education, offering a rigorous, inquiry-based program that cultivates curiosity, academic excellence, leadership, teamwork, and resilience, preparing students to become confident, lifelong leaders who flourish in an ever-evolving world.

## Letter from the Head of School Stephanie Medcalfe

![Image 4: Stephanie Medcalfe Image](https://3.files.edl.io/e447/26/05/29/214714-2d396dfc-fbb5-4f61-b910-f026a8ab6ca1.png)

I am delighted to introduce you to Virginia Chance School, where we prioritize not only strong academic achievement but also the overall development of your child.

We excel at creating a collaborative environment that instills self-motivation, a growth mindset, and critical thinking skills in our students.

Our focus on nurturing a love of learning through hands-on exploration and teamwork, in engaging classrooms and on a beautiful wooded campus, is ideal for children ready for the unique rigor of the Chance School.

Choosing the right educational path for your child is a significant decision, and I invite you to experience firsthand the captivating educational opportunities that await your child at Chance School.

Together, we can foster a lifelong love of learning and personal growth.

At Chance, we embrace a progressive education approach that is evidence-based and recognized for its innovative, inquiry-focused curriculum. The curricular foundation blends the school’s philosophy with age-appropriate milestones, Common Core Standards, and guidelines from our accrediting bodies, ISACS, NAEYC, the Gesell Institute, and academic best practices.

Each day, your child will have the opportunity to explore, discover, and develop meaningful connections with their peers and the world around them. Welcome! We can't wait to get to know your family and share what makes Virginia Chance School so magical!

Better Together  
  
There is something special that happens when children gather. One child has an idea, another sees it differently. Someone asks a question no one else had thought to ask. A quiet voice finds the confidence to speak, while another child learns that listening can be just as important as being heard.  
  
Together, they build, create, problem solve, wonder and sometimes disagree. And somewhere is the middle of it all, something beautiful happens: the learning becomes bigger than any one child could have created alone.   
  
That lesson doesn’t stop at the classroom door. It is woven into the very heart of the Chance community.   
  
A school is more than the children sitting in its classrooms. It is the teachers who pour their hearts into creating meaningful experiences. The families who cheer from the sidelines. The staff who make each day possible. The alumni who carry their experiences with them. The friends, grandparents, and neighbors who believe in the kind of childhood we are creating together.   
  
That is what makes Give for Good so meaningful. It’s not simply about giving to a school, it is about investing in the moments that make a Chance childhood possible - the muddy boots, the curious questions, the friendships and the moments when a child suddenly realizes I CAN DO THIS.   
  
Every gift becomes part of that story. Together we can make a difference, together we are Chance. ✨

What makes a Chance School teacher different?   
  
It is in the way they nurture a child’s spirit while igniting their curiosity.  
  
It is in the way they pause to listen to each child’s voice, knowing that every thought, question, and idea deserves to be heard.   
  
It is in the way they involve children in their own learning, inviting them to wonder, explore, touch, create, and bring ideas to life.   
  
It is in the language they use: words that encourage reflection and make space for personal choice.   
  
Because at Chance, we believe education is not about telling children what to think. It is about giving them the confidence, curiosity and courage to discover how to think.   
  
And perhaps that is where the magic of a Chance teacher truly lies - in their remarkable ability to guide each child toward discovering the answers, ideas, and possibilities that are already waiting within. ✨

At the beginning of a new school year one of the most important things a teacher can do is get to know the child behind the learner.   
  
What brings them joy? What do they wonder about? Who and what do they love? What experiences have shaped their little world?  
  
One beautiful way we begin this journey at Chance is through - Heart Maps. Inviting children to draw and write about the people, places, memories, passions and dreams they carry in their hearts.   
  
Heart Maps open a window into each child’s world and helps teachers build meaningful relationships, create connections and design meaningful learning experiences that shape their teaching.   
  
Before children can fully engage in learning, it is important for them to know that they are truly seen and valued, not just for what they can do, but for what lives inside their hearts ❤️

At Chance, we believe that education is about so much more than what a child knows. It is about who they are becoming.   
  
A child arrives at school each morning carrying a whole world with them - their questions, their friendships, their worries, their dreams and their unique way of seeing the world. To educate the whole child is to see and nurture all of those pieces.   
  
Because children do not leave their hearts at the classroom door.   
  
A whole child approach begins with the understanding that learning happens best when children feel known, valued, connected and safe to be themselves.   
  
At Chance we make room for it all. We nurture the thinkers, creators, problem solvers and adventurers. We value academic growth while understanding that academic success does not happen in isolation. It grows alongside confidence, resilience, empathy and a genuine love of learning.   
  
Sometimes whole child education can look like a child sitting quietly absorbed in a book and sometimes it can look like muddy hands exploring the natural world. And sometimes, perhaps most importantly, it looks like a teacher noticing the child who needs encouragement.  
  
This is the beauty of a whole child approach: we are not simply preparing children for the next grade or the next test. We are helping them develop skills that will carry with them throughout their lives, in a climate of rapid change. Childhood is not simply preparation for life, childhood is life. Our doors are always open ✨

Tales from Under the Trees   
  
Beneath a canopy of whispering leaves, a pitcher of sunshine-yellow lemonade became an act of kindness, imagination, and wonder. To an adult, it may look like simple play. To a child, it is storymaking.  
  
Storymaking is how children make sense of their world. It allows them to explore ideas, emotions, relationships, and adventures in a way that feels natural and joyful. When children create imaginary worlds, characters, and adventures, they are weaving together experiences, strengthening problem- solving skills, developing empathy, and nurturing creativity. Through imagination, they discover that they are not merely participants in the world—they are creators within it. Through these small moments, children become authors of their own learning.  
  
And perhaps most importantly, storymaking preserves something precious: the ability to believe that the world is full of possibilities.  
  
The lemonade was not for friends or family; it was for a bear. The child had never actually seen the bear. No pawprints marked the ground, and no rustling shape moved between the trees. Yet the child knew what it liked to drink and how thirsty it might be.  
  
Whether the bear ever comes is beside the point. The magic was already there, the moment the child believed it might be.  
  
Last week, our Summer Under the Trees camp was transformed into a world of wonder and imagination as children stepped into the role of Enchanted Explorers.  
  
With colorful ribbons dancing in the breeze, little hands crafted magical wands ready for woodland adventures. Nearby, a busy lemonade stand appeared, serving refreshing drinks to the "forest bears" who had wandered into our imaginary world. Fairy wings fluttered as children twirled, danced, and celebrated the magic of summer beneath the trees.  
  
At Virginia Chance School, we believe childhood is a time for curiosity, creativity, and joyful discovery. Through imaginative play and meaningful experiences in nature, children create stories, build friendships, and develop a deeper connection to the world around them.

Discovering the Secret Sounds of Plants  
  
🌿✨ Have you ever wondered if plants can "speak"? During a recent exploration, children asked, "Do flowers have a sound?" Instead of giving a quick answer, we embraced their curiosity with a magical journey using PlantWave technology.  
  
PlantWave lets us listen to the subtle electrical signals of plants, transforming them into music! 🎶 Our students were excited to share their theories on how a dead plant might sound compared to a living one. From no sound to slow, melodious tunes to lively, happy beats, their imaginations ran wild.  
  
They wondered what else around us might be communicating in ways we can’t see or hear and requested to go around our campus and discover what else could make music! We made so many beautiful discoveries. Moments like this remind us that the world is more alive than we often realize.🌱💡  
  
This lesson was a blend of science and imagination, encouraging young minds to think beyond what they can see or hear and to remain open to the wonders of nature. 🌞

Embracing the Elements: What It Means to Be a 'Chance Kid' 🌧️🎒  
Remember the joy of splashing in puddles or playing in the mud as a child? Whether you loved it or hesitated at the thought of wet socks, these moments shaped us. At Chance School, we believe in creating these core memories for our Chance Kids and building resilience along the way.  
  
Tough Temperatures Build Resilience ❄️  
This winter taught us a lot! Our gear kept us warm, but frigid temperatures tested our limits. At times, friends would come up right away to ask, "When are we going inside?" While we want to be sure children are safe, we allow for moments of discomfort and flexibility, giving our friends ideas of how they can stay warm on a cold day through racing, climbing, and laughing.  
  
Messy Conditions Build Flexibility 🌿  
Our friends have grown through messy, outdoor play. A wet sock in a boot? No problem, just pull that boot off and ditch the sock. Just remember to bring it inside with you. Speaking of inside, teachers learn flexibility too, with helping to transition from outerwear once inside. We learn to take it in stride and make time for the cleanup. It can add stress, but we breathe through it and, more importantly, laugh through it.  
  
Living With a Little Discomfort Teaches Patience 🌧️  
On days when the temperatures are safe for getting wet (we look forward to a lot more of these in the springtime), we push ourselves to live in the moment and cherish the learning that only happens when you stop controlling the elements and start embracing them. Dry clothes are waiting for us inside, thanks to our thoughtful Moms and Dads. We are safe. Let's feel how those drops of rain coat our hair and sprinkle in our eyes.  
  
A Special Thank You to the Missing Socks 🧦  
To all the missing socks, mittens, and hats- thank you for being part of our journey. While we do our best to reunite you with your owners, sometimes you become little heroes lost in the adventure. Keep labeling, and we'll keep looking!  
  
Join us in celebrating the resilience, flexibility, and patience of our Chance Kids as we continue to make memories, one raindrop at a time. 🌈- Pre-K Teachers Ms. Julia & Ms. Brooke

Building Trust 🌟  
An excerpt from a Preschool Threes Newsletter:  
  
"Trust is all about consistency! When expectations are not consistent, children can become easily confused. This confusion will lead to them testing more boundaries and even power struggles. It is important that we set clear expectations for what is expected versus unexpected behavior at a given place or time. This is work that we start on day one and take very seriously because we understand the why behind it. As teachers and parents, it is our job to be the constant. This means we must follow through with what we say will happen in a certain situation. This is how we build trust.  
  
Consistency is Key:  
  
Lunch: Encourage keeping hands to themselves. “Bothering friends or touching their food is not a good choice, we will have to find a more successful spot for you to sit. We keep our hands to ourselves at lunch.”  
  
Outdoor Play: Safety first! “It is not safe when you poke someone with a stick, show us the safe way to play with sticks or they will be closed to you.”  
  
At school, unless it's a serious safety concern, we give two reminders before any consequences. Following through is crucial - empty words break trust.  
  
Follow Through with Few Words:   
  
“Not safe. Sticks are closed now.”  
  
Acknowledge feelings: “I know you’re sad, but sticks are closed. Try again tomorrow.”  
  
At lunch, after reminders: “I’m going to help you find a more successful spot to eat.”  
  
Our forever hope is that when we share this kind of information with you, it helps support your hard work at home. Preschool Teachers- Ms. Jensen & Ms. Katie"

The Power of How We Speak: A Journey in Tone  
  
🌟 Room 1 Pre-K Update: Embracing the Power of Tone 🌟  
This week, we embarked on an exciting journey to understand the importance of our tone of voice. Our children have been doing an amazing job expressing their big feelings with words. Now, we’re focusing on how to deliver those words with care and empathy.  
  
Discovering the Meaning of "Tone"  
Before diving in, we asked the children what "tone" means to them. Here are their insightful thoughts:  
“It’s the way your words sound.” — Camden  
“It’s how you hear it and feel it.” — Ace  
“Sometimes it’s too loud.” — Roman  
“It’s how you know someone is happy or mad.” — Walker  
  
As our young learners grow, so do their communication skills. At ages 4 and 5, they are learning the art of using their words thoughtfully. A loud or unkind tone can unintentionally upset others, turning small issues into big ones.  
  
Listening Beyond the Words  
To illustrate the power of tone, we role-played scenarios. We used the phrase, “Hey, you broke my train track!” in two different tones: one angry and one calm. The children noticed the difference:  
“When you yelled, it made me not want to listen.” — Rihaan  
“They were the same but they made me feel different.” — Remi  
“When you said it happy, it made me feel happy and calm.” — Roman  
“The mean tone made me feel scared.” — Ella  
“Yeah, the loud tone made me feel shy.” — Davis  
We encouraged them to try using different tones, facial expressions, and body language, learning that how we say something can change the meaning, even if the words remain the same.  
  
Moments of Love, Play, and Careful Communication  
In moments of frustration, we emphasized awareness over correction, using gentle reminders like “tone check” and “redo!” This empowers the children to recognize the power of their words and offers them a chance to express themselves as they truly intend to.

## Ursuline Core Values

  
Our Core Values of Reverence, Service, Leadership, and Community are woven together to empower the Sacred Heart community to live Christ-centered lives rooted in the Catholic faith and Ursuline tradition.  
  
  
Reverence is at the heart of our actions resulting in mindful relationships built with compassion. We act with an abiding respect for God, ourselves, each other, and all of creation.  
  
Service is born of reverence. It calls us to be intentional stewards and advocates who contribute to our common home and family. We collaborate with those we serve to address needs, making the world a better place.  
  
Leadership is an act of service that positively shapes the community. We act as leaders by compassionately serving the needs of others, being risk-takers that go beyond expectations, and seeking to inspire.  
  
Community is a fellowship of support and connection, where we call each other by name while serving our neighbors, peers, and the world through inclusivity, listening, and bridge-building.  
  
Together, we celebrate our love for God, our diverse family, and our work in education as we strive to become globally minded, compassionate leaders.  
  
**Authentically Catholic. Proudly Ursuline.**  
  
From its founding by the Ursuline Sisters in 1877 as the Academy of the Sacred Heart, Sacred Heart Schools has been creating enlightened scholars, compassionate leaders of high character, and responsible citizens who make a difference across Kentucky and around the world.  
  
Sacred Heart Schools provides an International Baccalaureate and Cognia-accredited, Catholic, Ursuline education from early childhood through high school and offers community-wide after-school arts instruction and performances. We transform nearly 2,000 students' lives yearly through Catholic faith formation, academic excellence, leadership development, art exploration, athletic growth, and service outreach.  
  
**Authentically Catholic**  
We are rooted in the Gospel of Jesus Christ and the teaching mission of the Catholic Church.  
We are dedicated to building community and offering education that affirms and enhances the dignity of all individuals.  
  
Through our common connection as members of God's family, we celebrate diversity and reverence all people. Our inclusive culture enables all students, faculty, and staff to develop and thrive while sharing their God-given talents.  
  
**Proudly Ursuline**  
Founded in 1877 and sponsored by the Ursuline Sisters of Louisville, we are a Catholic, Ursuline community.  
Sacred Heart Schools is mission-driven and guided by the Ursuline Charism of St. Angela Merici - a contemplative love of God and a resulting openness and eagerness to serve the needs of others.  
  
We are committed to teaching and living the Ursuline Core Values of reverence, service, leadership, and community.

## Ursuline Core Values

  
Our Core Values of Reverence, Service, Leadership, and Community are woven together to empower the Sacred Heart community to live Christ-centered lives rooted in the Catholic faith and Ursuline tradition.  
  
  
Reverence is at the heart of our actions resulting in mindful relationships built with compassion. We act with an abiding respect for God, ourselves, each other, and all of creation.  
  
Service is born of reverence. It calls us to be intentional stewards and advocates who contribute to our common home and family. We collaborate with those we serve to address needs, making the world a better place.  
  
Leadership is an act of service that positively shapes the community. We act as leaders by compassionately serving the needs of others, being risk-takers that go beyond expectations, and seeking to inspire.  
  
Community is a fellowship of support and connection, where we call each other by name while serving our neighbors, peers, and the world through inclusivity, listening, and bridge-building.  
  
Together, we celebrate our love for God, our diverse family, and our work in education as we strive to become globally minded, compassionate leaders.  
  
**Authentically Catholic. Proudly Ursuline.**  
  
From its founding by the Ursuline Sisters in 1877 as the Academy of the Sacred Heart, Sacred Heart Schools has been creating enlightened scholars, compassionate leaders of high character, and responsible citizens who make a difference across Kentucky and around the world.  
  
Sacred Heart Schools provides an International Baccalaureate and Cognia-accredited, Catholic, Ursuline education from early childhood through high school and offers community-wide after-school arts instruction and performances. We transform nearly 2,000 students' lives yearly through Catholic faith formation, academic excellence, leadership development, art exploration, athletic growth, and service outreach.  
  
**Authentically Catholic**  
We are rooted in the Gospel of Jesus Christ and the teaching mission of the Catholic Church.  
We are dedicated to building community and offering education that affirms and enhances the dignity of all individuals.  
  
Through our common connection as members of God's family, we celebrate diversity and reverence all people. Our inclusive culture enables all students, faculty, and staff to develop and thrive while sharing their God-given talents.  
  
**Proudly Ursuline**  
Founded in 1877 and sponsored by the Ursuline Sisters of Louisville, we are a Catholic, Ursuline community.  
Sacred Heart Schools is mission-driven and guided by the Ursuline Charism of St. Angela Merici - a contemplative love of God and a resulting openness and eagerness to serve the needs of others.  
  
We are committed to teaching and living the Ursuline Core Values of reverence, service, leadership, and community.

## Welcome to JCPS!

We have fantastic elementary schools in Jefferson County Public Schools (JCPS). Each of our 89 elementary schools offers engaging, effective teaching in a caring, supportive environment. We offer a variety of learning opportunities through unique schools, programs, and activities that will inspire your student to reach their fullest potential.

This booklet will help you learn about the special offerings that each individual school can provide your student and family. Every JCPS school has dedicated and experienced teachers, technology for every student, family support services, and engaging after-school programming. They all contribute to our students’ sense of belonging as we teach them core skills like reading and math. But students are also introduced to art, music, other languages, and social skills as they learn to communicate and flourish in a constantly changing world.

Please take the time to review the multitude of offerings we have available, and determine how they align with the learning style and interests of your student.

At JCPS, our mission is to always do what’s best for our students. We hope this booklet will help you determine what’s best for your student.

## Let’s Get Started

The Jefferson County Public School (JCPS) District has **89 elementary schools**, all of which focus on core subjects like reading, writing, math, science, and social studies while also introducing students to a variety of other subjects, such as the arts, technology, and world languages.

To better predict your student’s educational path, JCPS is moving away from “clusters” and now designates elementary school zones by high school networks.Each elementary school is grouped into **1 of 15 feeder patterns**—groups of 3 to 8 JCPS elementary schools located within a geographic area connected to a specific JCPS high school. JCPS guarantees your student a seat at one of the schools in their designated zone, determined by your student’s home address.JCPS also offers students living in the Choice Zone an option to attend school close to home or farther away.

While most elementary school students choose to attend one of the schools in their zone, JCPS has other programs to best match your student’s learning style or interests.We offer a variety of elementary magnet schools and magnet programs—many of which are nationally recognized or focus on a specialized area.

# Register & Apply

### Review Options and Select Preference

Decide what type of learning environment works best for your student, and explore school options, programs, and/or offerings at each school.

During the application process, you will be asked to rank schools in your designated zone by order of preference. You can also apply for up to two other options, such as a magnet school or a school-based magnet program.

Enrolling in school is a two-step process.

1.Register for JCPS if you are a new student.

2.Complete the Elementary Application.

### Elementary School Options

#### Zone Schools (page 8)

*   Current JCPS students will be automatically enrolled in their resides school. New JCPS students who have already registered with the district and would like to attend their resides school should contact the school (not the Office of School Choice) to enroll.

#### Magnet Schools (page 68)

*   You can attend either your close-to-home option or the school designated for your address that is far away. This is only for incoming sixth graders, middle school students new to the district, or middle school students with a new address in the Choice Zone. An application is required to make your selection.

#### Magnet Programs (page 76)

*   If your preference is outside of your resides school boundary, you can select and apply for up to two magnet schools or programs.

#### Traditional Magnet Schools* (page 41)

*   If you are currently enrolled in a JCPS Traditional Magnet elementary school, no application is necessary. You will be automatically enrolled in the Traditional Magnet middle school that serves your home address.

_*You must apply to a Traditional Magnet middle school if you are not currently enrolled in a Traditional Magnet elementary school._

## Have You Registered?

**You need to register if:**

*   Your student has never attended a JCPS school.

**How to Register**

*   Online

*   At any JCPS middle school

*   At the Office of School Choice

**Registration Process**

*   All students new to JCPS must register with the district before applying for school. You can register at any time. Students who are currently enrolled in JCPS Early Childhood do not need to register again.

*   You may register your student for school regardless of immigration status and/or a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence. For more information, contact the Office of Access and Opportunity at **(502) 485-3650**.

**After You Register**

After you register, JCPS will verify your information and send you an email to complete your application, which can take up to two business days. Incoming kindergartners and/or new students to JCPS may then apply to schools within their zone. To find out which zone you’re located in, call the JCPS Demographics Office at **(502) 485-3050** or use the online JCPS SchoolFinder search tool. (See page 4 to scan QR code.)

## Apply

**Dates to Remember**

*   Applications open: **November 3, 2025**

*   Application deadline:**December 19, 2025**

*   Acceptance notification: **April 2026**

**You need to apply if:**

*   Your student has never attended a JCPS school.

*   Your student has had a change of address.

*   Your student is applying for a magnet school or magnet program.

**Application Process**

**Important to note:** It’s important to reference the on-time application window. We accept late applications; however, space at your preferred school(s) may be limited based on school capacity.

All elementary students completing an application must rank the schools within their zone in order of preference. If you live in the Choice Zone, you must select between your close-to-home or far-away options before you begin ranking. JCPS keeps siblings together in elementary school zones. The district also considers parental choice, space, a student’s home address, and the diversity of the student body when placing students at schools. Due to capacity constraints, not all families can or will receive their first school choice.

**Magnet Application Information**

*   Students may submit one magnet application per year.

*   Submitting a magnet application doesn’t guarantee admission, and submitting false information will void an application.

*   Waiting lists are not kept from year to year.

*   Magnet applications can only be edited during the on-time application period.

*   Siblings of current or former magnet school students do not receive preference in the application process, but those who share the same date of birth (twins, triplets, etc.) are treated as one application. However, parents must submit a separate application for each student.

**How to Apply**

What magnet schools are in the district?

There are five districtwide elementary magnet schools. These schools accept students from across the district and do not fall within a zone.

*   **Brandeis Elementary** offers the Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) Magnet, engaging students in Project-Based Learning (PBL) opportunities.

*   **J. Graham Brown School** is a Self-Directed Learning school, encouraging reasoned minds and educated hearts through independence, empathy, innovation, and advocacy.

*   **Coleridge-Taylor Montessori Elementary**offers the Montessori Program. This self-directed learning fosters rigorous, self-motivated growth in all areas of development.

*   **Hawthorne Elementary** is the only Spanish Immersion Magnet in JCPS. Every student who comes to Hawthorne will experience a Spanish Immersion learning environment in all grades.

*   **Lincoln Elementary Performing Arts School (LPAS)** is Kentucky’s only public elementary magnet school focused on the performing arts.

JCPS also has five boundary-based magnet elementary schools, **Audubon**,**Carter**, **Foster**,**Greathouse/Shryock**,**and Schaffner**, offering the Traditional Program as their magnet. Eligibility is dependent on your student’s home address. The Traditional Magnet Program provides a student-centered and rigorous academic curriculum in a highly structured learning environment that is essential for developing College and Career Readiness. The Traditional Program contributes to a student’s growth by emphasizing high academic standards and responsible conduct. In addition, the traditional program develops character and leadership skills through community involvement and promotes student well-being.

Our focus as Traditional schools is placed on the core subjects with an emphasis on developing complex thinkers who are self-directed learners and problem solvers striving for individual excellence and reaching their fullest potential in Academics, Character, and Citizenship.

## Welcome to JCPS!

We have fantastic elementary schools in Jefferson County Public Schools (JCPS). Each of our 89 elementary schools offers engaging, effective teaching in a caring, supportive environment. We offer a variety of learning opportunities through unique schools, programs, and activities that will inspire your student to reach their fullest potential.

This booklet will help you learn about the special offerings that each individual school can provide your student and family. Every JCPS school has dedicated and experienced teachers, technology for every student, family support services, and engaging after-school programming. They all contribute to our students’ sense of belonging as we teach them core skills like reading and math. But students are also introduced to art, music, other languages, and social skills as they learn to communicate and flourish in a constantly changing world.

Please take the time to review the multitude of offerings we have available, and determine how they align with the learning style and interests of your student.

At JCPS, our mission is to always do what’s best for our students. We hope this booklet will help you determine what’s best for your student.

## Let’s Get Started

The Jefferson County Public School (JCPS) District has **89 elementary schools**, all of which focus on core subjects like reading, writing, math, science, and social studies while also introducing students to a variety of other subjects, such as the arts, technology, and world languages.

To better predict your student’s educational path, JCPS is moving away from “clusters” and now designates elementary school zones by high school networks.Each elementary school is grouped into **1 of 15 feeder patterns**—groups of 3 to 8 JCPS elementary schools located within a geographic area connected to a specific JCPS high school. JCPS guarantees your student a seat at one of the schools in their designated zone, determined by your student’s home address.JCPS also offers students living in the Choice Zone an option to attend school close to home or farther away.

While most elementary school students choose to attend one of the schools in their zone, JCPS has other programs to best match your student’s learning style or interests.We offer a variety of elementary magnet schools and magnet programs—many of which are nationally recognized or focus on a specialized area.

# Register & Apply

### Review Options and Select Preference

Decide what type of learning environment works best for your student, and explore school options, programs, and/or offerings at each school.

During the application process, you will be asked to rank schools in your designated zone by order of preference. You can also apply for up to two other options, such as a magnet school or a school-based magnet program.

Enrolling in school is a two-step process.

1.Register for JCPS if you are a new student.

2.Complete the Elementary Application.

### Elementary School Options

#### Zone Schools (page 8)

*   Current JCPS students will be automatically enrolled in their resides school. New JCPS students who have already registered with the district and would like to attend their resides school should contact the school (not the Office of School Choice) to enroll.

#### Magnet Schools (page 68)

*   You can attend either your close-to-home option or the school designated for your address that is far away. This is only for incoming sixth graders, middle school students new to the district, or middle school students with a new address in the Choice Zone. An application is required to make your selection.

#### Magnet Programs (page 76)

*   If your preference is outside of your resides school boundary, you can select and apply for up to two magnet schools or programs.

#### Traditional Magnet Schools* (page 41)

*   If you are currently enrolled in a JCPS Traditional Magnet elementary school, no application is necessary. You will be automatically enrolled in the Traditional Magnet middle school that serves your home address.

_*You must apply to a Traditional Magnet middle school if you are not currently enrolled in a Traditional Magnet elementary school._

## Have You Registered?

**You need to register if:**

*   Your student has never attended a JCPS school.

**How to Register**

*   Online

*   At any JCPS middle school

*   At the Office of School Choice

**Registration Process**

*   All students new to JCPS must register with the district before applying for school. You can register at any time. Students who are currently enrolled in JCPS Early Childhood do not need to register again.

*   Students must be a resident of Jefferson County to register. If families are relocating, contact the Office of School Choice at **(502) 485-6250**.

*   You may register your student for school regardless of immigration status and/or a fixed, regular, and adequate nighttime residence. For more information, contact the Office of Access and Opportunity at **(502) 485-3650**.

**After You Register**

After you register, JCPS will verify your information and send you an email to complete your application, which can take up to two business days. Incoming kindergartners and/or new students to JCPS may then apply to schools within their zone. To find out which zone you’re located in, call the JCPS Demographics Office at **(502) 485-3050** or use the online JCPS SchoolFinder search tool. (See page 4 to scan QR code.)

## Apply

**Dates to Remember**

*   Applications open: **November 3, 2025**

*   Application deadline:**December 19, 2025**

*   Acceptance notification: **April 2026**

**You need to apply if:**

*   Your student has never attended a JCPS school.

*   Your student is entering kindergarten.

*   Your student has had a change of address.

*   Your student is applying for a magnet school or magnet program.

**Application Process**

**Important to note:** It’s important to reference the on-time application window. We accept late applications; however, space at your preferred school(s) may be limited based on school capacity.

All elementary students completing an application must rank the schools within their zone in order of preference. If you live in the Choice Zone, you must select between your close-to-home or far-away options before you begin ranking. JCPS keeps siblings together in elementary school zones. The district also considers parental choice, space, a student’s home address, and the diversity of the student body when placing students at schools. Due to capacity constraints, not all families can or will receive their first school choice.

**Magnet Application Information**

*   Students may submit one magnet application per year.

*   Submitting a magnet application doesn’t guarantee admission, and submitting false information will void an application.

*   Waiting lists are not kept from year to year.

*   Magnet applications can only be edited during the on-time application period.

*   Siblings of current or former magnet school students do not receive preference in the application process, but those who share the same date of birth (twins, triplets, etc.) are treated as one application. However, parents must submit a separate application for each student.

**How to Apply**

Families are encouraged to apply online (scan QR code), but in-person application options are available.

You can apply in person at the following locations:

*   JCPS Office of School Choice: 4309 Bishop Lane

*   Any school location

## Elementary School Zones

**Fast Facts**  
Application required

**What is a zone?**  
A zone is a group of three to eight JCPS elementary schools located within a specific geographic area connected to a specific JCPS high school. This will better predict your student’s educational path. JCPS guarantees every student a seat at a school in their zone, which is determined by their home address.

Incoming kindergarten students, students new to JCPS, or students with an address change must complete an application.

All students may also apply for magnets, magnet programs, and school transfers.

### Choice Zone

Students living within the Choice Zone (black outline) have the choice to attend the assigned elementary school that is close to home or a school that is farther away.

Incoming kindergarten students, students new to JCPS, or students with an address change in the Choice Zone must complete an application to rank their close-to-home or far-away school selections. All students may also apply for magnets and transfers.

## Feeder Patterns

JCPS has developed 15 feeder patterns that allow parents to see the elementary, middle, and high school their student will attend based on their home address.

Percentages represent the portion of the student body to attend the indicated high school.

**Magnet Schools**

Fast Facts Application required

What magnet schools are in the district?

There are five districtwide elementary magnet schools. These schools accept students from across the district and do not fall within a zone.

*   **Brandeis Elementary** offers the Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts, and Mathematics (STEAM) Magnet, engaging students in Project-Based Learning (PBL) opportunities.

*   **J. Graham Brown School** is a Self-Directed Learning school, encouraging reasoned minds and educated hearts through independence, empathy, innovation, and advocacy.

*   **Coleridge-Taylor Montessori Elementary**offers the Montessori Program. This self-directed learning fosters rigorous, self-motivated growth in all areas of development.

*   **Hawthorne Elementary** is the only Spanish Immersion Magnet in JCPS. Every student who comes to Hawthorne will experience a Spanish Immersion learning environment in all grades.

*   **Lincoln Elementary Performing Arts School (LPAS)** is Kentucky’s only public elementary magnet school focused on the performing arts.

JCPS also has five boundary-based magnet elementary schools, **Audubon**,**Carter**, **Foster**,**Greathouse/Shryock**,**and Schaffner**, offering the Traditional Program as their magnet. Eligibility is dependent on your student’s home address. The Traditional Magnet Program provides a student-centered and rigorous academic curriculum in a highly structured learning environment that is essential for developing College and Career Readiness. One in 10 secondary schools in Norfolk are currently rated “outstanding” - but all are facing a fresh inspection as Ofsted works to update grades that were handed out several years ago. The latest data available shows that, as of the end of March, five state-run secondary schools in Norfolk had been awarded Ofsted’s highest rating of “outstanding”.

Those five secondary schools are Hethersett Academy, Ormiston Victory Academy, Ormiston Venture Academy, Notre Dame High School and Wymondham College.

They are among 551 outstanding secondary schools in England. But only 95 of those outstanding schools - and none in Norfolk - have been inspected since the pandemic, from June 2021. The rest had not been visited by Ofsted inspectors for a full graded inspection since they were first awarded the highest status - in some cases as long ago as 2007.

That is mainly because outstanding primary and secondary schools were exempt from routine inspection between 2012 and 2020. Visits to schools from Ofsted inspectors were then paused for 18 months during the pandemic, with the watchdog now working to clear the backlog.

In Norfolk, 10% of state-run secondary schools are currently rated outstanding. Of the rest 71% are classed as “good”, 15% “require improvement” and 4% are “inadequate”.

Since routine inspections have resumed, Ofsted says it has so far completed graded inspections of 739 formerly exempt primary and secondary schools. Of those, 134 (18%) have remained “outstanding”. Previously exempt schools that have gone longest without inspection have been prioritised, an average of 13 years.

Ofsted says that means they are not “typical of all exempt schools, and the pattern of inspection outcomes may change later”. Ofsted expects to have completed inspections of all previously exempt outstanding schools by the end of July 2025.

A spokesperson for Ofsted said: “Our inspections are first and foremost for children and their parents – looking in depth at the quality of education, behaviour, and how well and safely schools are run. We always want inspections to be constructive and collaborative and in the vast majority of cases school leaders agree that they are.”

Staff at Yaxham Church of England Primary School are celebrating following its recent Ofsted inspection, which raised its rating from a school 'requiring improvement'to 'good'. The report comes after a two-day visit in January after its two previous reports in May 2019 and December 2016. [](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en) Headteacher Jennie Müller and chair of governors Michelle Parnell were delighted to share the outcome of the inspection, saying in a joint statement: “We are so proud of the progress we have made as a [school](https://www.derehamtimes.co.uk/news/education/), which is down to the hard work and dedication of everyone within the school community. “It comes at the perfect time, as we begin the next phase of our journey in joining the Diocese of Norwich Education and Academies Trust.” ![Image 6: Dereham Times: Yaxham Church of England Primary School](https://www.derehamtimes.co.uk/resources/images/16549438.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)Yaxham Church of England Primary School _(Image: Denise Bradley)_ READ MORE:[_**Lyng Church of England Primary joins DNEAT as 38th member**_](https://www.derehamtimes.co.uk/news/23174787.lyng-church-england-primary-joins-dneat-38th-member/) The chair of the governors at the school, near[Dereham](https://www.derehamtimes.co.uk/local-news/dereham-news/),sent a letter of thanks to the community, adding: ”It has been a sometimes rocky path, littered with difficult decisions and some very tough conversations not to mention a global pandemic. “However, one thing that has always been true is the desire to make sure that every single child will flourish and achieve and that is so very obviously apparent when you speak to staff, children, governors, parents and carers past and present. “Our amazing team at Yaxham have always given their all and I want to thank each and every one of them for giving so much and continuing to do so. They all have so much passion and work so hard to ensure that our children receive the best experiences while they are at school.” Ofsted praised the school's positive relationships between pupils and staff, a “broad and ambitious curriculum”and how well children with special educational needs and/or disabilities are supported. # Ofsted and Performance Data

## Ofsted Inspections

[Include Norfolk](https://www.compare-school-performance.service.gov.uk/school/134440/include-school-norfolk/2021/secondary)is monitored by Ofsted. The school was last fully inspected in May 2023, and received a ‘**Good**’ rating.

## OFSTED report May 2023- Rating GOOD

*   [10286133 - Include School Norfolk - 134440 Final PDF.pdf](https://www.includenorfolk.org.uk/_site/data/files/migrated/ofsted-and-performance-data/10286133-include-school-norfolk-134440-final-pdf.pdf)

## Monitoring inspection report March 2023

*   [Include School Norfolk.pdf](https://www.includenorfolk.org.uk/_site/data/files/migrated/ofsted-and-performance-data/include-school-norfolk.pdf)

**Please read the report in full, however highlights from the report are:**

"Pupils join the school after having profoundly negative experiences at other schools. They receive the support they need to heal and positively engage with education. Pupils learn about themselves and how to manage their emotions and behaviour positively. Pupils are supported well to value their potential and meet the high expectations of them. They are determined to be successful in adult life and are well prepared for their next steps in education or training. The positive ethos at the school enables pupils to develop strong relationships with staff and each other. On arrival each morning, pupils respond well to staff’s smiley and optimistic greetings. This continues throughout the rest of the day. Pupils look out for each other and work well together. When relationships become strained, pupils are equipped to find their own positive solutions. On the rare occasions of bullying, or when pupils are unable to resolve friendship issues, they are well supported so that problems stop and do not re-occur. Pupils are safe at school. They appreciate that staff support them when they are worried about issues at school, at home or in the community."

*   [OFSTED Inspection reports](https://reports.ofsted.gov.uk/provider/27/134440)

## Parent and Carer Feedback

Parents and carers are encouraged to give feedback about the school to Ofsted directly, using the[Ofsted Parent View questionnaire](https://parentview.ofsted.gov.uk/).

Results for 2019/20 were affected by the Covid-19 pandemic. Since they were based on teacher-based assessments they are not comparable with previous years. Accurate comparable results will be published as soon as they are available.

## Student Results

*   [Education - KS4 Achievements Report.pdf](https://www.includenorfolk.org.uk/_site/data/files/migrated/ofsted-and-performance-data/education-ks4-achievements-report.pdf)  
  
[Achievement Data Norfolk 2024 / 2025](https://www.includenorfolk.org.uk/_site/data/files/24994A090FA5275F2551404407EBA7B9.pdf)

## DfE Performance Tables

Information about Catch22 school performance can be found on the[Department of Education school and college performance website](https://www.compare-school-performance.service.gov.uk/school/134440/include-school-norfolk/secondary).

It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. The report card for a north Norfolk school has jumped a grade - from ‘inadequate’ straight to ‘good’. Staff, pupils and family members at Antingham and Southrepps Primary School are delighted about the positive rating, which has been awarded by Ofsted following an inspection on March 9. ![Image 6: Eastern Daily Press: Antingham and Southrepps Primary School pupils taking part in an outdoor activity](https://www.edp24.co.uk/resources/images/16782485.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)Antingham and Southrepps Primary School pupils taking part in an outdoor activity _(Image: Sonya Duncan)_ [](https://www.outbrain.com/what-is/default/en) Miles Elcock, who has been the school’s headteacher since April last year, said he was "overjoyed". **READ MORE:[Norfolk singer's big hopes for her girl band's debut single](https://www.northnorfolknews.co.uk/news/22786930.norfolk-singers-big-hopes-girl-bands-debut-single/)** Mr Elcock said: “The community, the staff and the children all deserve it for the hard work they’ve put in. It shows that the proof is in the pudding and we’re making the right decisions.” ![Image 7: Eastern Daily Press: Antingham and Southrepps Primary School pupils jumping for joy, pictured with head teacher Miles Elcock](https://www.edp24.co.uk/resources/images/16782507.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)Antingham and Southrepps Primary School pupils jumping for joy, pictured with head teacher Miles Elcock _(Image: Sonya Duncan)_ The school has 56 pupils from nursery to Year 6 aged three to 11. The education watchdog rated it ‘requires improvement’ in October 2017, and it then fell back to ‘inadequate’ in March 2020. ![Image 8: Eastern Daily Press: Antingham and Southrepps Primary School head teacher Miles Elcock](https://www.edp24.co.uk/resources/images/16782521.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)Antingham and Southrepps Primary School head teacher Miles Elcock _(Image: Sonya Duncan)_ The school has now bypassed the middling grade to be classed as ‘good’, Ofsted’s second highest grade, below ‘outstanding’. Mr Elcock added: “It’s been a journey. We have a really nice Antingham family feel which has always been part of the school.” **READ MORE:[Solar panel car parts to be installed at The Reef, Sheringham](https://www.northnorfolknews.co.uk/news/23522566.solar-panel-car-parts-installed-reef-sheringham/)** He said the school offered regular excursions to destinations such as London, the Royal Norfolk Show and local beaches, and had two dogs - one for reading and another for therapy. ![Image 9: Eastern Daily Press: Antingham and Southrepps Primary School](https://www.edp24.co.uk/resources/images/16782538.jpg?type=mds-article-575%20575w)Antingham and Southrepps Primary School _(Image: Sonya Duncan)_ It also has a free breakfast club and after-school activities including dodgeball and bushcraft. ## Disclaimer

All data on this page is sourced from the Department for Education’s 2024/2025 Compare School Performance dataset. It includes state-funded and, where available, independent secondary schools. Please note that Progress 8 scores were not published by the DfE for the 2024/25 academic year, as this cohort did not have Key Stage 2 prior attainment data due to pandemic-related assessment cancellations.

Some schools may also be missing data for GCSE 9–7 results or Ofsted ratings due to unpublished or unavailable figures. Rankings are based only on schools with published data and may not reflect recent changes. Please check school websites for the latest information.

## How we ranked the best schools in Norfolk?

Why trust our rankings? Our analysis is based on the latest 2024/2025 data from the Department for Education’s Compare School Performance (CSP) database, which publishes official performance data for all secondary schools in England, including both state-funded and independent schools where available.

We’ve created separate tables to highlight top performers in three key areas:

*   **Progress 8** (pupil progress from KS2 to GCSE)
*   **GCSE 9–7 grades** (academic excellence)
*   **Overall school listings**, with available Ofsted ratings

Schools are primarily ranked by their **Progress 8** score. This clever metric doesn’t just reward schools with high-attaining intakes – it highlights the ones that genuinely support student growth by measuring progress from the end of primary school to GCSEs. It adjusts for prior attainment, making it one of the fairest ways to compare schools.

Where available, we also show the percentage of GCSE grades at 9–7 to reflect high academic achievement, and Ofsted ratings for added context. All figures come directly from CSP’s official dataset.

Where Progress 8 data is not available for any schools in Norfolk, the corresponding table will not be shown. This simply means that no schools in this area had published Progress 8 scores at the time of the latest dataset, it does not reflect on the quality of the schools themselves.

## How to support your child at home

Helping your child succeed at school doesn’t just happen in the classroom, the right support at home can make a big difference. Encourage a regular study routine, provide a quiet space for learning, and take an interest in what they’re covering in lessons. Even small actions, like checking in on homework or discussing what they learned that day, can build motivation and accountability.

If you’re looking for extra structure, our[GCSE Revision Resources](https://www.savemyexams.com/gcse/) are designed to make studying easier. With expert-written notes, topic-by-topic exam questions, and mark schemes, your child can practise exactly what they need to know, when they need to know it.

## Boosting confidence before exams

Confidence can make a huge difference to exam performance. Start by helping your child identify their strengths and weaknesses, then focus revision time on areas that need improvement. Practising under timed conditions can reduce exam-day nerves, while celebrating small wins along the way builds self-belief.

Our [GCSE Exam Practice](https://www.savemyexams.com/gcse/) pages include hundreds of past-paper style questions and worked solutions, so students can walk into their exams knowing exactly what to expect. By building familiarity with the question styles and formats, they’ll feel prepared and ready to perform at their best.

## FAQs - best secondary schools in Norfolk

### What is the highest-rated secondary school in Norfolk?

Based on the latest Department for Education CSP data, the highest-rated secondary school in Norfolk is Norwich School by GCSE 9–7 results. In the case of an exact tie across these measures, the first school in alphabetical order is shown here. For full details and to compare all schools, please refer to the performance tables above.

### Are private schools included in this list?

No. This guide covers state-funded secondary schools only, including grammar, comprehensive, academy, and free schools. Independent/private schools are not included in our rankings.

### What’s the best way to apply for schools in Norfolk?

Applications are usually managed by Norfolk County Council. You can find deadlines, admissions policies, and catchment area maps on the council’s official website.

### How can I compare schools near me?

Use Ofsted inspection reports, the Department for Education’s CSP performance tables, and our rankings to compare schools side by side. Visit schools during open days for first-hand impressions.

### How can I compare schools near me?

Ofsted rates secondary schools as Outstanding, Good, Requires Improvement, or Inadequate. Outstanding secondary schools excel in teaching quality, student behaviour, leadership, and outcomes.

### What is a good Progress 8 score for secondary schools in Norfolk?

A Progress 8 score above 0 means students make better progress than the national average. Scores above +0.5 indicate well above average progress, while top-performing secondary schools typically achieve +0.7 or higher. The best schools in Norfolk consistently score above +0.8.

## Disclaimer

All data on this page is sourced from the Department for Education’s 2024/2025 Compare School Performance dataset. It includes state-funded and, where available, independent secondary schools. Please note that Progress 8 scores were not published by the DfE for the 2024/25 academic year, as this cohort did not have Key Stage 2 prior attainment data due to pandemic-related assessment cancellations.

Some schools may also be missing data for GCSE 9–7 results or Ofsted ratings due to unpublished or unavailable figures. Rankings are based only on schools with published data and may not reflect recent changes. Please check school websites for the latest information.

## How we ranked the best schools in Norfolk?

Why trust our rankings? Our analysis is based on the latest 2024/2025 data from the Department for Education’s Compare School Performance (CSP) database, which publishes official performance data for all secondary schools in England, including both state-funded and independent schools where available.

We’ve created separate tables to highlight top performers in three key areas:

*   **Progress 8** (pupil progress from KS2 to GCSE)
*   **GCSE 9–7 grades** (academic excellence)
*   **Overall school listings**, with available Ofsted ratings

Schools are primarily ranked by their **Progress 8** score. This clever metric doesn’t just reward schools with high-attaining intakes – it highlights the ones that genuinely support student growth by measuring progress from the end of primary school to GCSEs. It adjusts for prior attainment, making it one of the fairest ways to compare schools.

Where available, we also show the percentage of GCSE grades at 9–7 to reflect high academic achievement, and Ofsted ratings for added context. All figures come directly from CSP’s official dataset.

Where Progress 8 data is not available for any schools in Norfolk, the corresponding table will not be shown. This simply means that no schools in this area had published Progress 8 scores at the time of the latest dataset, it does not reflect on the quality of the schools themselves.

## How to support your child at home

Helping your child succeed at school doesn’t just happen in the classroom, the right support at home can make a big difference. Encourage a regular study routine, provide a quiet space for learning, and take an interest in what they’re covering in lessons. Even small actions, like checking in on homework or discussing what they learned that day, can build motivation and accountability.

If you’re looking for extra structure, our[GCSE Revision Resources](https://www.savemyexams.com/gcse/) are designed to make studying easier. With expert-written notes, topic-by-topic exam questions, and mark schemes, your child can practise exactly what they need to know, when they need to know it.

## Boosting confidence before exams

Confidence can make a huge difference to exam performance. Start by helping your child identify their strengths and weaknesses, then focus revision time on areas that need improvement. Practising under timed conditions can reduce exam-day nerves, while celebrating small wins along the way builds self-belief.

Our [GCSE Exam Practice](https://www.savemyexams.com/gcse/) pages include hundreds of past-paper style questions and worked solutions, so students can walk into their exams knowing exactly what to expect. By building familiarity with the question styles and formats, they’ll feel prepared and ready to perform at their best.

## FAQs - best secondary schools in Norfolk

### What is the highest-rated secondary school in Norfolk?

Based on the latest Department for Education CSP data, the highest-rated secondary school in Norfolk is Norwich School by GCSE 9–7 results. In the case of an exact tie across these measures, the first school in alphabetical order is shown here. For full details and to compare all schools, please refer to the performance tables above.

### Are private schools included in this list?

No. This guide covers state-funded secondary schools only, including grammar, comprehensive, academy, and free schools. Independent/private schools are not included in our rankings.

### What’s the best way to apply for schools in Norfolk?

Applications are usually managed by Norfolk County Council. You can find deadlines, admissions policies, and catchment area maps on the council’s official website.

### How can I compare schools near me?

Use Ofsted inspection reports, the Department for Education’s CSP performance tables, and our rankings to compare schools side by side. Visit schools during open days for first-hand impressions.

### How can I compare schools near me?

Ofsted rates secondary schools as Outstanding, Good, Requires Improvement, or Inadequate. Outstanding secondary schools excel in teaching quality, student behaviour, leadership, and outcomes.

### What is a good Progress 8 score for secondary schools in Norfolk?

A Progress 8 score above 0 means students make better progress than the national average. Scores above +0.5 indicate well above average progress, while top-performing secondary schools typically achieve +0.7 or higher. The best schools in Norfolk consistently score above +0.8.

## Made by Girls

Made by girls is our way of celebrating the **bold, curious and confident** young people who make our school what it is.

We believe our role as an all-girls independent high school in Norwich, Norfolk, is to provide the best possible environment for our students to be themselves – and that their successes are testament to girls having a place of their own in which to thrive.

Where they are **supported, celebrated and pushed forward** by each other.

Where they can **speak up** without fear of judgement – **play** without fear of ridicule – **learn without limits**.

When you [visit us](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/admissions/visits-and-tours/) we’re sure you’ll feel the difference it makes to be in a place for girls and **Made by girls**.

## Why girls only?

**Girls and boys are equal – but they’re not the same**. How they grow and learn is different.

Evidence suggests that in a girls only school, girls:

*   are less likely to conform to gender stereotypes,
*   are less constrained in their subject choices,
*   show a greater propensity to take risks and innovate,
*   perform better in exams,
*   have more opportunities to show leadership, and
*   are more successful in the job market.

Here at the only all-girls private school in Norwich, girls are given every opportunity, without prejudice, to **explore and fulfil their potential**.

Choosing an independent girls’ school like Norwich High School For Girls means providing an education that’s tailored to how girls learn best, at every stage—from [nursery](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/early-years/welcome/) and [prep](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/prep-school/welcome/), to [senior school](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/senior-school/welcome/), [sixth form](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/sixth-form/welcome/) and beyond.

[Read more](https://www.gdst.net/publications/why-and-how-girls-thrive-in-girls-only-schools/ "Read more")

## Visit us

The best way to experience one of the top private girls’ schools in Norfolk—from nursery and prep, through to senior school and sixth form—is to visit us in person.

We hold a variety of Open Events throughout the year when you can explore our spaces and support, and meet the wonderful students and teachers who make Norwich High School for Girls so special.

If you would prefer, we can **arrange a tour on a date and time of our high school to suit you**. We can also prepare a [taster day](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/admissions/join-our-school/) for your daughter so she can start to make new friends and experience what life is really like at this at this award-winning private school for girls in Norwich.

## Made by Girls

Made by girls is our way of celebrating the **bold, curious and confident** young people who make our school what it is.

We believe our role as an all-girls independent high school in Norwich, Norfolk, is to provide the best possible environment for our students to be themselves – and that their successes are testament to girls having a place of their own in which to thrive.

Where they are **supported, celebrated and pushed forward** by each other.

Where they can **speak up** without fear of judgement – **play** without fear of ridicule – **learn without limits**.

When you [visit us](https://www.norwichhigh.gdst.net/admissions/visits-and-tours/) we’re sure you’ll feel the difference it makes to be in a place for girls and **Made by girls**.
